page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-80 is an x86_64 virtual instance powered by Intel Xeon processors operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The server provisions 80 virtual CPUs derived from 40 physical cores via hyper-threading, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 640 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU distribution suitable for memory-heavy operations. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, requiring attached block storage for persistent data and omitting hardware-accelerated graphics or matrix engines.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-quartile multi-core compute and memory performance alongside average to modest single-core execution. The platform achieves strong multi-threaded ratings across Geekbench multi-core (16,164.0), PassMark CPU (52,733.77), and multi-core stress-ng tests. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 321.39 GB/sec read and 145.01 GB/sec write throughput. Additionally, the instance delivers high throughput in application benchmarks, sustaining over 74 million Redis SET operations per second and 64.0 GB/sec in static web serving. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as single-core stress-ng fall into lower percentiles, and large language model text generation metrics remain constrained across CPU-only inference tests.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-core density provides resource alignment for workloads bound by memory limits rather than raw single-thread clock rates. Primary tradeoffs involve relying completely on remote storage and absorbing lower single-thread efficiency. The configuration fits enterprise in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency static web serving, large-scale Clang software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data transformation workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-80 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 Intel Xeon processors running at 2.8 GHz. It provides 80 dedicated vCPUs across 40 physical cores with hyper-threading, accompanied by 640 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark results show strong parallel processing and memory throughput, highlighted by high multi-core stress-ng scores, Geekbench multi-core performance, and Redis operation throughput exceeding 74 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU execution sits lower in relative rankings, and LLM text generation rates remain low due to CPU-based inference constraints. Given its massive RAM allocation and strong multi-threaded capabilities, n2-highmem-80 is well configured for in-memory databases, large Redis caches, memory-intensive data processing pipelines, software compilation tasks, and high-throughput static web serving.
